reviews.title: What Did I Pay For?

I may as well have downloaded the full MyNetDiary and subscribed which I would have done. Have a just paid four quid merely to investigate your app?? And no invoice, so no refund!

reviews.text:
This is pretty much the light+ version of the free version

You’re pretty much just buying a demo for their premium service. If I had known this, I would have just gotten any other calorie tracking app

reviews.title: I’m disappointed
reviews.text:
I’m disappointed with the app’s behavior and monetization design. Even after disabling subscription reminders and premium prompts, the app still constantly suggests features that turn out to be Premium-only after you tap them. This is frustrating and feels misleading.

Premium-only features should either be clearly marked everywhere or fully hidden when the user chooses to disable Premium promotions. I don’t need AI tools, advanced analytics, or any of the extra premium clutter. I just want a clean food diary and recipe tracker without endless upsell attempts.

The food database for Russia is also very poor compared to competitors.

Overall, the experience feels unnecessarily pushy and overcomplicated for users who only need basic calorie and recipe tracking.

reviews.title: Hard to navigate
reviews.text: Very hard to navigate. If you pay for the extra recipe packs, the recipe seem to be hidden somewhere. Not easy to jump, back-and-forth between logging your meals and looking at recipes

reviews.title: Meal scanner
reviews.text: I don’t think that the AI photo of your food is an accurate count of calories when I weigh it versus actually just taking a picture. It’s pretty different.

reviews.title: Diet made easy
reviews.text: This used to be great but now it can’t find the easiest foods. I’m on the verge of moving but it’s got 2 years of data.

reviews.title: Scam!
reviews.text: Ask for one off payment £3.99 and when you pay they then let you know to get the full benefits of the app you must upgrade waste of time!

reviews.title: Nags you to upgrade
reviews.text:
I thought by purchasing the Pro version of the app it’d stop constantly nagging me to upgrade.

My mistake. I’m still seeing banners and pop-ups cluttering my app.

They are very clever and don’t show them all the time — for example a banner has now appeared after a few days.

This company uses lots of FOMO dark patterns to entice upgrading such as ‘one-time only offers’ and ‘one-day sales’.

It just feels like extracting money from my pocket is the primary goal and I’m not having it. I’ve requested a refund and I also have decided not to upgrade to Premium (I was considering it) because, guess what, there’s also a Premium PLUS and I’m sure I’ll just get nagged to upgrade to that.

reviews.title: Not good.

reviews.title: Dissapointed
reviews.text:
As a Premium continuous client of 5 years, I am deeply disappointed to notice that as soon as I paused my annual subscription, my old app records and past data are no longer available - although I paid for that period of time. Past data retrieved based on a full paid subscription should be available to a client indefinitely, simply because they paid for it. 
Someone could take the time to sue you for such a thing!
Also, I bought the Pro version, back in 2020, the Pro app that is still available to buy in Apple App Store at the same price. The App is supposed to track 108 nutrients. After pausing my Premium subscription I should have had active the Pro features, which does not happen. 
Again, no respect for your customers.
